Americans who need assistance: call 24/7 at +1-202-501-4444 (from abroad) and +1-888-407-4747 (from the U.S. and Canada) Alerts for U.S. Citizens Read alerts for U.S. Citizens Emergency Assistance Local Emergency Information and Contacts Visit Travel.State.gov for More Information Close ⨉ Help us improve United States Partners with ODPM To Enhance Disaster Response Capacity Through $250,000 Humanitarian Assistance Project By U.S. Embassy Trinidad & Tobago 4 MINUTE READ November 18, 2026 Left to right: Shaina Khan Regional Coordinator ODPM, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Defence Narine Charran, U.S. Embassy Acting Deputy Chief of Mission Michael Fitzpatrick, Cpt Leah Lee U.S. Embassy, Dennis Marcelle Operations Manager ODPM Participants observe a live demo of the newly installed video wall system   PORT OF SPAIN, Trinidad and Tobago, November 18, 2026 – The United States Government has completed a capacity-building project valued at more than US$250,000 to support Trinidad and Tobago’s disaster preparedness and emergency response capabilities. Through the United States Embassy and the United States Southern Command’s (USSOUTHCOM) Humanitarian Assistance Program, the project provided specialized training for 30 personnel from the Office of Disaster Preparedness and Management (ODPM) and upgraded the technology and infrastructure at its Emergency Operations Centre (EOC). The project had two phases. In early June, 30 ODPM personnel completed training in critical emergency response protocols and systems, including the DisasterAWARE platform, the Incident Command System (ICS) and the Management of Mass Casualty Incidents (MCI). The second phase involved equipping the EOC with technology and infrastructure to support information sharing and emergency monitoring. The installations include a video wall system, video conferencing technology, computer workstations, office furniture and integrated communications equipment. The United States and Trinidad and Tobago marked the project’s completion on November 18 at a handover ceremony at the EOC in Mausica. Acting U.S. Embassy Deputy Chief of Mission Michael Fitzpatrick highlighted the project’s connection to the longstanding cooperation between the two countries. “In 2017, USSOUTHCOM partnered with the Government of Trinidad and Tobago to construct the ODPM Emergency Operations Centre. Today, we build on that foundation through continued collaboration that has provided both specialized training and critical equipment to strengthen ODPM’s ability to protect lives and coordinate effective emergency response. “Disasters do not recognize borders, and the strength of any response depends on preparation, coordination, and trusted partnerships.” Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Defence Narine Charran highlighted the importance of disaster preparedness to national security and public safety. “Strengthening disaster preparedness is an investment in national security and the protection of our people. This contribution from the United States Government will enhance the ODPM’s capacity to monitor emerging threats, coordinate emergency operations and respond more effectively when it matters most. We value this enduring partnership and our shared commitment to building a safer, stronger and more resilient Trinidad and Tobago, and Caribbean region.” The project reflects ongoing bilateral cooperation between the United States and Trinidad and Tobago. education , U.S. Southern Command Deputy Chief of Mission , News , Security U.S. Embassy in Trinidad & Tobago White House Department of State Privacy Policy Social Media Terms of Use Contact us FOIA No Fear Act Accessibility Statement Freedom 250 Cookie Settings We use cookies to make our website work better and improve your experience.
